title: Install Prereqs Audit Suite for Private VPC Deploys
creator: Ayesha Malik
description: Goal: Provide an automated, idempotent audit suite that validates environment prerequisites for Redwood Private (VPC) installs across AWS/GCP/Azure. The suite will surface quota shortfalls, IAM misconfigurations, DNS/resolver problems, GPU capacity and compatibility risks, Terraform backend/access issues, and basic networking misalignments prior to attempting an install or upgrade. Intended users: platform engineers running new customer installs and SRE/SEs verifying upgrade paths for existing customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A CLI/terraform data-source that performs the checks and exits non-zero if any critical requirement is unmet.
2) Checks cover quotas (service quotas, vCPU, GPUs, ENIs), IAM roles/policies and cross-account access, private DNS/resolver reachability, GPU instance family availability and driver compatibility, Terraform backend and S3/GCS/Azure Blob write/read permissions, and required VPC networking (subnet CIDR, route tables, NAT/Egress).
3) Output is machine-readable (JSON) and human-friendly with remediation links and suggested API calls/commands.
4) Integrated as a step in the private install CI pipeline and referenced by the onboarding runbook.
5) Tests (unit + integration mock) exercising failure modes for quotas, missing roles, DNS failures, and GPU shortages are present in the repo.
tasks: Define canonical checklist mapping to cloud provider APIs and service quotas
Implement provider-specific probes (AWS/GCP/Azure) using CLI SDKs and Terraform data-sources
Add GPU compatibility matrix check for common instance families and driver versions
Create JSON output schema and human-friendly formatter
Add remediation guidance and Confluence links for each failure type
Wire the audit into the private install pipeline as a mandatory pre-step
Create unit and integration tests including mocked quota failures
steps: Run read-only queries against cloud provider APIs to gather quotas/capacity: compute quotas, GPU quotas, ENI limits, VPCs per region
Validate IAM: existence of service roles, assumed-role permissions, KMS key policies, and ability to create/attach instance profiles
Test Terraform backend access: read/write to S3/GCS/Azure Blob, lock/unlock behavior for DynamoDB/Storage Table
DNS checks: confirm private hosted zone attachments, resolver endpoints, and forwarder reachability from a temporary probe instance in the target VPC

GPU availability: list compatible instance types in region, run short driver compatibility probe against selected AMIs/container images (non-destructive), verify CUDA/cuDNN minimal version requirements
Network sanity: verify subnet CIDR sizes, route table associations, NAT gateway presence for outbound access, required VPC endpoints (S3/ECR) are present
Upgrade compatibility: compare target cluster node image/kernel and required drivers; flag potential driver/kernel mismatches that could block upgrades
implementation_notes: We will implement as a small Go binary and Terraform external data-source. The binary will have cloud-provider pluggable modules and output both exit codes and JSON. Prefer read-only API usage; where transient resources are needed (resolver probe), create a short-lived instance with tags and a strict TTL. For AWS, use Service Quotas + DescribeAccountAttributes + DescribeInstanceTypeOfferings. For GPUs, consult instance type availability and optionally the provider capacity API (if available) to estimate spot/ondemand availability. Store remediation templates per failure type to be surfaced in console and CLI.
remediation_templates: Quota shortfall: workflow to request quota increase with links and example aws-cli/gcloud commands; IAM missing: example role/policy snippets and minimum required permissions; DNS failure: steps to attach private hosted zone or configure resolver rules; GPU shortage: suggested instance families and fallback policy to use quantized or smaller model variant
testing_plan: Unit tests for each probe module. Integration tests using mocked provider responses in CI. End-to-end smoke in a sandbox account verifying JSON output and CLI return codes. Add nightly synthetic test that runs the audit against a known good sandbox and fails the build if regressions detected.
